questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance from each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from each other.
questions.explanation: In a group, riders should use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while still maintaining safe distances.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Make an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: A parked motorcycle should make an angle with the curb between 45 and 90 degrees. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: If you lock your rear brake on a good road surface, you should:

options.text: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear wheel on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop. On a good surface, you can control the motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel as long as it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so you are visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: A front wheel wobble or sudden shaking of the handlebars is usually caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
The front wheel not being attached tightly to the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: Wobbling happens when the front wheel and handlebars shake from side to side. This is usually caused by improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: An engine will seize because of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not enough oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when oil runs low. Without oil, engine parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have better control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast causes a rider to lose control. The motorcycle may drift into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: To be seen better on the road, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when visibility is low.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to make sure others see your motorcycle is to ride with your headlight on all the time.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: A DOT-approved helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality helmet that fits properly is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then edge forward to see cross traffic.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to look better.
Stop at the stop line, then go through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then edge forward to see cross traffic.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop line or sign, stop where marked. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean your body forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Limit how many hours you ride per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how many hours you ride per day.
questions.explanation: On a long trip, take frequent breaks to rest, even if you don't feel tired. Most experienced riders don't ride more than six hours a day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tired faster, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when it gets wet.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing while riding at any time of day.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these can affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol consumed
questions.explanation: The three main factors that affect blood alcohol content (BAC) are how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane behind a car lets the driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as much as their rearview mirror.
Wind may make the side mirror useless.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as much as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver will most likely see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create space ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create space ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, ride in a way that encourages them to pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other motorists that you are riding near them.
Help other motorists see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other motorists that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other motorists that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. Flash your brake light before slowing for a sharp turn or where drivers may not expect you to slow down.

questions.question: Mirrors on motorcycles:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because motorcycles are smaller than cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding is to:

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead constantly. Watch for hazards so you can react to them before you reach them.

questions.question: To make it easier for others to see you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Brightly-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you, day or night.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet or icy pavement, gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Turn just your head to look through a turn. Keep your shoulders and eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal when you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and immediately pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly and ride straight. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Exit the road once your motorcycle has slowed down.
